payload.executive_summary: Candidate B1B implements a monolithic CLI pipeline (O1) to convert a local directory of Markdown notes into a fully static website with tags, backlinks, and client-side full-text search. The plan follows a thin-slice milestone strategy: Milestone 1 delivers a working CLI skeleton that ingests Markdown, renders HTML, and produces a deployable static site. Subsequent milestones layer tag extraction and tag pages (M2), internal link resolution and backlinks (M3), client-side search (M4), and polish items including broken-link warnings, base-URL configuration, GFM extensions, and cross-browser QA (M5). Key risks around link conventions (K2) and tag conventions (K3) are front-loaded into Milestones 2–3 via explicit configuration requirements. Scale risks (K4/K5) are deferred given the confirmed 1,000-note target. Privacy risk (K8) is accepted with documentation-only mitigation. The architecture keeps all processing in a single in-memory pipeline for simplicity, with clear component boundaries (C1–C8) that can be refactored later if extensibility demands grow.

architecture_choice.rationale: O1 (monolithic CLI pipeline) is the best fit for this project's focused scope, single-user orientation, and desire for fast time-to-value. It satisfies every MUST requirement with the least upfront design overhead. The single-process, in-memory approach is well within performance limits for the confirmed 1,000-note scale (R22). The main trade-off—limited extensibility compared to O2's plugin architecture—is acceptable because the project's non-goals explicitly exclude features that would demand a plugin ecosystem (e.g., multi-user, AI generation, mobile apps). O3 (SSG wrapper) was rejected because it couples the project to an external SSG's release cadence and makes standalone distribution harder. O4 (multi-stage pipeline with intermediate artifacts) adds complexity for incremental builds that are only a COULD requirement (R23).
architecture_choice.high_level_dataflow: CLI Orchestrator (C1) → Source Scanner & Front Matter Parser (C2) discovers .md files and parses front matter → Content Analyzer & Graph Builder (C3) extracts links, tags, and builds the in-memory NoteGraph with backlinks → Markdown Renderer (C4) converts each note to HTML → Template & Theme Renderer (C5) produces per-note pages, tag index, per-tag pages, home page, and all-notes listing → Search Index Builder (C6) generates a serialized full-text index from the NoteGraph → Output Emitter (C7) writes HTML pages, search index, and static assets to the output directory → Client-Side Runtime (C8) loads the search index in the browser and provides interactive search UI.

milestones.name: CLI Skeleton + Markdown Ingestion + Single-Note HTML Render

deliverables.text: CLI entry point accepting input directory and output directory arguments (R5)
Recursive .md file discovery from the input directory (R1)
CommonMark-compliant Markdown-to-HTML rendering for each discovered note (R3, R4)
Static site output directory containing one HTML page per note plus minimal CSS (R2)
Graceful per-file error handling for malformed YAML front matter (K6) and clear build error messages (R6)

exit_criteria: AT1 passes: three nested .md files discovered, non-.md excluded
AT2 passes: output contains only static assets and renders when served statically
AT3 passes: one-to-one mapping of non-excluded .md files to HTML pages
AT4 passes: headings, lists, emphasis, links, images, code blocks preserved in HTML
AT5 passes: CLI accepts input/output paths, exits 0, output directory created
AT6 passes: valid input succeeds; invalid input yields non-zero exit and actionable error

Tag normalization pipeline (case-folding, trimming) applied consistently (R16 SHOULD)
Per-note tag display with navigable links to tag pages (R12)
Tags index page and per-tag listing pages (R13)

exit_criteria: AT11 passes: tags extracted per configured convention and associated with correct notes

AT13 passes: tags index page lists all tags; per-tag pages list correct notes

milestones.name: Internal Link Resolution + Backlinks

deliverables.text: Standard Markdown relative link resolution to generated HTML pages (R9)
Backlinks section on each linked-to note page listing all source notes with clickable links (R10)
Link convention configuration supporting optional wiki-link syntax (R15 SHOULD)
Graph consistency checks for circular links and duplicate-title edge cases (K9, K10)

exit_criteria: AT9 passes: relative link in note-a navigates to note-b HTML page
AT10 passes: note-c shows backlinks from note-a and note-b, each clickable

milestones.name: Client-Side Search Index and Search UI

deliverables.text: Build-time full-text search index generation from note titles and body content (R8)
Client-side search UI that queries the prebuilt index entirely in-browser (R7)
Search results link to corresponding note pages

exit_criteria: AT7 passes: search returns correct results for body and title queries with no server requests
AT8 passes: search index artifact present in output and loaded by client-side search

milestones.name: Polish — Broken-Link Warnings, Base URL, GFM, Browser QA, Navigation

deliverables.text: Build-time warnings for unresolved internal links with source file and link text; non-navigable rendering of broken links (R18 SHOULD)
Configurable base URL / path prefix for subdirectory deployment (R19 SHOULD)
GFM extensions: tables, strikethrough, task lists, fenced code with syntax highlighting (R21 SHOULD)

R21 verified: GFM tables, strikethrough, task lists, and syntax-highlighted code render correctly

decision_log.question: Which architecture option should be selected?
decision_log.rationale: O1 provides the simplest end-to-end build flow, is easiest to package as a single CLI tool, and performs well for the confirmed 1,000-note scale. The project's focused scope and explicit non-goals (no plugins, no server runtime, no multi-user) make the extensibility trade-off acceptable.
alternatives_considered: O2 — Plugin-based build core: higher upfront complexity for extensibility not required by current scope
O3 — Existing SSG wrapper: couples to external SSG cadence; harder standalone distribution
O4 — Multi-stage pipeline with intermediate artifacts: adds complexity for incremental builds (R23 COULD)
what_would_change_this_decision: Requirement for third-party plugin ecosystem or community-contributed extensions
Need for incremental builds at scale beyond 1,000 notes becoming a MUST
Adoption of an existing SSG becoming a project constraint

evidence_pointers.quote: Straightforward end-to-end build flow and debugging (single CLI program)
simplest architecture that satisfies all MUST requirements with the least upfront design overhead

decision_log.question: What milestone delivery strategy should be used?
decision_log.choice: Thin-slice: each milestone produces a deployable static site with incrementally more features
decision_log.rationale: Thin-slice delivery de-risks integration issues by producing a working end-to-end artifact from Milestone 1. It enables early acceptance testing (AT1–AT6 after M1) and provides continuous feedback on build correctness.
alternatives_considered: Layer-cake: build all backend processing first, then add UI/templates — delays end-to-end validation
Feature-complete single release: higher integration risk and delayed feedback
what_would_change_this_decision: A hard deadline requiring all features simultaneously
Discovery that cross-cutting concerns (e.g., search index) cannot be added incrementally

evidence_pointers.quote: Each milestone produces a deployable static site with incrementally more features

decision_log.question: How should tag conventions be handled given unconfirmed Q2?
decision_log.choice: Support configurable tag sources (YAML front matter and inline #tags) with a normalization pipeline (case-fold, trim)
decision_log.rationale: Making tag source configurable addresses the uncertainty in Q2 while satisfying R11 (user-selectable convention) and R16 (normalization). The normalization pipeline mitigates K3.
alternatives_considered: Support only YAML front matter tags — simpler but excludes inline #tag users
Support only inline #tags — misses structured front matter metadata
what_would_change_this_decision: Confirmed answer to Q2 specifying a single convention
Discovery of a third tagging convention (e.g., nested tags) requiring additional parsing

evidence_pointers.quote: at least one supported tagging convention that is user-selectable/configurable

evidence_pointers.note: K3 risk on undefined tag conventions
evidence_pointers.quote: Tag extraction conventions and normalization are undefined/inconsistent

decision_log.question: How should internal link conventions be handled given unconfirmed Q1?
decision_log.choice: Default to standard Markdown relative links (R9 MUST); add configurable wiki-link support (R15 SHOULD) in M3
decision_log.rationale: Standard relative links are the minimum MUST requirement. Wiki-link support is layered as a SHOULD to address the high-impact uncertainty in Q1 and mitigate K2 without blocking M1.
alternatives_considered: Support only relative links — leaves wiki-link users unsupported
Support wiki-links from the start — increases M1 complexity before conventions are confirmed
what_would_change_this_decision: Confirmed answer to Q1 specifying wiki-links as the primary convention
Discovery that the note collection uses Obsidian-style links exclusively

evidence_pointers.note: R9 MUST for relative link resolution
evidence_pointers.quote: correctly resolve standard Markdown relative links to other Markdown notes

evidence_pointers.note: R15 SHOULD for additional link syntaxes
evidence_pointers.quote: support additional link syntaxes beyond standard Markdown relative links

decision_log.question: How should scale/performance risks (K4, K5) be handled?
decision_log.choice: Defer active mitigation; accept in-memory approach for confirmed 1,000-note target
decision_log.rationale: The monolithic in-memory pipeline (O1) is well within performance limits for 1,000 notes. K4 and K5 mitigations (streaming, chunked index loading) would add complexity without benefit at this scale. R22 SHOULD performance target (500 ms search) is validated in M4.
alternatives_considered: Implement streaming/chunked processing from the start — over-engineering for current scale
Choose O4 multi-stage pipeline for caching — unnecessary complexity
what_would_change_this_decision: Performance testing in M4 revealing search latency exceeding 500 ms at 1,000 notes

evidence_pointers.quote: build process becomes unacceptably slow, crashes, or hangs
up to 1,000 notes on a modern consumer device, full-text search results SHOULD be returned and rendered in under 500 ms

decision_log.question: How should the privacy leakage risk (K8) be handled?
decision_log.choice: Accept with documentation-only mitigation: build-time warning banner and README disclaimer
decision_log.rationale: Access control is an explicit non-goal. The user is the primary stakeholder and is responsible for deployment decisions. A build-time warning and README disclaimer provide adequate notice without adding authentication complexity that contradicts the project's constraints.
alternatives_considered: Add optional .noteignore for sensitive files — useful but does not prevent intentional publishing of sensitive content
Require explicit publish confirmation — adds friction without solving the root issue
what_would_change_this_decision: Project scope expanding to include shared/public deployment as a primary use case
Regulatory requirement for access control on published content

evidence_pointers.quote: Sensitive/private information contained within notes is inadvertently published

evidence_pointers.note: Branch risk posture accepts K8 with documentation
evidence_pointers.quote: Accept K8 (privacy leakage) with documentation-only mitigation

decision_log.question: How should XSS risk (K7) be mitigated?
decision_log.choice: Enable HTML sanitization by default in the Markdown renderer; disable raw HTML pass-through unless explicitly opted in
decision_log.rationale: Default sanitization prevents XSS from note content without requiring user action. Users who trust their content can opt in to raw HTML via configuration. This aligns with the security-by-default principle and mitigates K7.
alternatives_considered: Allow raw HTML by default — higher XSS risk for shared deployments
Strip all HTML unconditionally — too restrictive for power users
what_would_change_this_decision: Confirmed single-user-only deployment with no sharing — could relax default
Discovery of Markdown content requiring raw HTML for core functionality

evidence_pointers.quote: XSS/content injection risk if note content (including raw HTML) is rendered into pages without proper sanitization

supplemental_evaluations.title: Acceptance Test Coverage for SHOULD Requirements
supplemental_evaluations.notes: The canonical acceptance tests (AT1–AT14) cover all MUST requirements but do not include dedicated tests for SHOULD requirements R15 (wiki-links), R16 (tag normalization), R17 (navigation), R18 (broken-link warnings), R19 (base URL), R20 (file exclusion), R21 (GFM), or R22 (search performance). Per the branch acceptance strategy and alignment warning AL001, additional acceptance tests for these SHOULD requirements should be authored before freeze. This candidate's milestones include exit criteria referencing these SHOULD requirements, but formal AT# tests are not yet defined.

evidence.note: AL001 flags missing tests for SHOULD requirements

supplemental_evaluations.title: Blocking Open Questions Impact Assessment
supplemental_evaluations.notes: Q1 (link conventions), Q2 (tag conventions), Q3 (scale), Q4 (information architecture), and Q10 (CLI vs GUI) are marked as blocking. This candidate assumes CLI (Q10 → R5), 1,000-note scale (Q3 → R22), and configurable conventions for Q1/Q2. Q4 is addressed by providing a default navigation structure (R17 SHOULD) with home, all-notes, tags index, and search. If confirmed answers contradict these assumptions, milestones M2–M5 may require rework.

synthesis_warnings.summary: No canonical acceptance tests (AT#) exist for SHOULD requirements R15–R22. Alignment warning AL001 recommends adding these before freeze. New AT# IDs are outside this role's minting authority.
Blocking open questions Q1, Q2, Q3, Q4, and Q10 remain unconfirmed. Assumptions are embedded in this candidate but confirmed answers may invalidate milestone scope or architecture choice.
